rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity in the closely spaced central cluster. The current last peak is comfortably below 10 minutes, so resolving the critical pairs is the priority.

Test a smaller temperature increase because warming improved the closest central pair but narrowed another gap. Holding the gradient fixed will show whether 55 C can resolve the cluster without creating a new overlap.

Use a shallower gradient at 50 C to improve the remaining close pair while avoiding the overlap that developed at 55 C. The last-peak time has enough margin to test increased separation without an expected time penalty.

Combine 55 C with a moderately shallower gradient: the slope change should widen the gap that became critical at 55 C, while retaining much of the temperature-induced separation in the other close pair. Twelve minutes balances these opposing selectivity trends and should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark and now seek a shorter fully resolved separation. Raising the starting organic fraction one step tests whether retention can be reduced without losing either marginally resolved pair.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope to recover the resolution lost at the higher starting organic fraction. This tests a narrower solvent window that may retain full resolution with a last-peak time close to, or slightly shorter than, injection 5.

Keep injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a cooler, steeper gradient for a shorter fully resolved alternative. The observed temperature-driven changes in elution order suggest that a different selectivity window may exist below 40 C.

Test a faster, high-temperature selectivity window, aiming to move the temperature-sensitive central pair through its crossover and separate it in reversed order. Injection 5 remains the fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the remaining central overlap separates further after its apparent elution-order reversal. This should also shorten retention, but the early pair and the neighboring central gap need monitoring.

Explore a moderately cooler selectivity window, where the central pair that crossed between 40 and 50 C may separate in the opposite order. The 12-minute gradient should help preserve neighboring separations while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a steeper gradient at 60 C to increase separation after the central elution-order crossover. Returning to the low starting organic fraction should protect the early pair and the neighboring central gap that deteriorated at phi0 = 0.20.

Preserve injection 5’s successful slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute while shortening the programmed gradient to 8 minutes. Its last peak eluted at 7.60 minutes, before this shortened gradient ends at the outlet, so the same fully resolved separation is expected.

Test whether a shallower gradient at 60 C restores the temperature-sensitive central gap while giving the other critical pair more resolution margin. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score benchmark; this run seeks a more robust fully resolved alternative with the last peak still expected below 10 minutes.

Refine the promising 55 C region with a slightly shallower gradient than injection 7 to bring its R = 1.47 pair above baseline resolution. The other critical pair retained some margin at this starting composition, so this may provide a more robust maximum-score method while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 50 C separates the critical central pair, since making the gradient shallower reduced its resolution. This explores a substantially faster alternative while retaining injection 5 as the shortest confirmed maximum-score method.

Refine the fully resolved 55 C region by pairing a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. This tests whether both critical pairs can gain resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Use a slope between injections 7 and 15 to seek full resolution with a shorter last-peak time than injection 15. The slightly shallower gradient should lift injection 7’s R = 1.47 pair above 1.5 while preserving the other critical gap.

Test a small slope increase from 0.075 to 0.080 per minute around the fastest fully resolved method. This should shorten the last-peak time and establish whether the critical pairs tolerate a modest acceleration.

Test whether lowering temperature at a higher starting organic fraction restores the early and central gaps that failed at 60 C. The moderate gradient slope may preserve enough central resolution to produce a faster fully resolved alternative; injection 5 remains the benchmark.

Lengthen injection 20’s gradient one step to test whether its two moderately unresolved pairs can reach baseline resolution while retaining a shorter elution time than injection 5. Monitor the closest pair carefully, since shallower gradients reduced its resolution at lower starting organic fractions.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity window and flatten injection 17’s gradient to improve its sole unresolved pair. The other critical pair had useful margin, and the last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, making this a candidate for a more robust maximum-score method.

Increase the endpoint one step to shorten injection 22’s separation while using its resolution margin. This intermediate slope should keep both critical pairs above 1.5 and reduce the last-peak time; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a slope of 0.065 per minute, between injection 7’s slightly unresolved separation and injection 18’s fully resolved result. This should shorten injection 18’s last-peak time while retaining full resolution; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving the successful slope through the critical peak cluster, then test whether the final hold elutes the last compound within 10 minutes. Injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved benchmark; this final run tests a narrower solvent window without disturbing the critical separations.
